forecast_results.prediction: TMF Holdings amalgamation will face material institutional opposition at 2nd AGM (June 29, 2026)
forecast_results.evidence: The AGM was held on 2026-06-29 as scheduled. Web-sourced coverage (dated around 2026-06-29/30) reports the AGM 'approved FY26 statements, dividend, Girish Wagh reappointment, and related-party transaction' -- i.e. a related-party-transaction resolution reportedly passed. This is suggestive that the vote was not blocked, but public search could not confirm (a) whether the approved RPT resolution is specifically the TMF Holdings-related item this forecast tracks (separate related-party items, including the Tata Cummins RPT flow flagged as RF-RPT-001, were also on the agenda), or (b) the actual vote margin / scrutinizer report needed to judge 'material institutional opposition' vs a routine supermajority pass. Marked not assessable rather than guessed, per CLAUDE.md S3 (no source = no claim).

lessons: Price action: TMCV rose from an entry_price of Rs369.15 (2026-06-07, S&P Capital IQ Key Stats export) to a web-sourced Rs422.20 close on 2026-07-10 (Kotak Neo / Alice Blue aggregation via search, most recent dated quote found; true 2026-07-13 close not independently located) -- a +14.37% absolute move in ~5 weeks, well above the NIFTY 50's +2.43% over a comparable window (NIFTY 50 23,631.75 close on 2026-06-12 to 24,207 close on 2026-07-10, both Investing.com/Business Standard-sourced, dated; June 12 used as the nearest located dated close to the 2026-06-07 decision date, not an exact match). Benchmark-relative return +11.94% is a NOTABLE positive move against the original Watchlist/no-position call.

sector_return_pct (NIFTY AUTO) is left null: a dated closing value was found for 2026-06-30 (26,250.40) but not for a date near the 2026-06-07 decision date or near the 2026-07-10/13 review date, so no like-for-like sector return could be computed without guessing -- left null per DECISION_LEDGER.md S8 rather than fabricated.

The rally happened WITHOUT the two things the original thesis flagged as decisive: the Iveco financing structure is still undisclosed (France/Spain approvals pending, deal not closed) and the TMF Holdings AGM outcome could not be confirmed in the specific terms the forecast tracked (vote margin / institutional opposition). This is a genuine tension: price outcome (strongly positive so far) has decoupled from thesis resolution (still unresolved on both binary risks) -- exactly the 'good process, bad luck OR too early' vs 'luck' distinction DECISION_LEDGER.md S10 exists to separate, and it cannot be resolved yet because neither binary has actually fired.

Data-pool access: this review ran without access to data/TMCV/ (gitignored, not present in this review environment); the AGM scrutinizer report and any post-decision NSE/BSE filings were sought only via public web search, which could not confirm the exact TMF Holdings vote percentage. A future review with pool access should pull the scrutinizer's report and the Q1 FY27 SIAM MHCV data directly.

No red flag has been resolved either way: RF-CAP-001 (Iveco), RF-RPT-002 (TMF Holdings), and the Filter 4 / Filter 6 S24 caps all still stand exactly as at decision -- the rating cap logic (max Watchlist until Iveco financing is resolved and minority-holder protection evidence exists) has not been triggered to lift.

module_calibration_notes.status: too early to attribute with confidence
module_calibration_notes.note: The valuation module's reverse-DCF (implied ~1.7% FCF CAGR priced in) and the +4.3% probability-weighted expected return look, so far, directionally too cautious given the +14.4% move -- but the move has occurred entirely on sentiment/momentum (strong June retail auto sales headlines industry-wide, plus the resolved-without-incident AGM) rather than on resolution of either named binary risk (Iveco financing, TMF opposition). It would be a process error to credit the valuation or catalyst modules with being 'wrong' this early: the killer risk (Iveco fully debt-funded close) has not been ruled in or out, and the module verdicts were explicitly conditioned on those two unresolved binaries. Re-assess at the 90d checkpoint (2026-09-05), which should capture Q1 FY27 results and the September NCD refinancing evidence.

memo_delta.summary: TMCV rallied ~14.4% (Rs369.15 -> ~Rs422.20 web-sourced) since the June 7 decision, ~12pp ahead of the NIFTY 50, even though neither of the thesis's two named binary risks has resolved: the Iveco deal remains unclosed (France/Spain regulatory approvals still pending) and the TMF Holdings AGM vote outcome could not be confirmed in the specific terms (vote margin, institutional opposition) the forecast ledger tracks. The rating cap (max Watchlist until Iveco financing is resolved and minority-holder protection evidence exists) has not been lifted by any new evidence -- the price move looks like sentiment/momentum, not thesis resolution, and is flagged as at-risk to monitor rather than acted upon.
memo_delta.stage_one_comment: TMCV is up about 14% since our June 7 Watchlist call, well ahead of the Nifty 50's roughly 2%. That is a real gap and worth flagging, but it has not been earned by resolution of either risk we said would move the rating: the Iveco Group deal is still not closed (France and Spain regulators have not signed off yet), and we could not confirm from public sources whether the TMF Holdings-related AGM vote on June 29 passed comfortably or with real institutional pushback -- coverage says a related-party resolution was approved, but not the margin. Nothing in the filings changed the ~80% downside case if Iveco closes fully debt-funded, and that risk is still live. We are treating this as the market getting ahead of an unresolved binary, not as confirmation we were wrong -- but the gap is now large enough that a materially lower entry point no longer exists if the binary resolves favorably, which cuts into the safety margin of waiting. We are not chasing the rally. Hold Watchlist; revisit hard at Q1 FY27 results and on any Iveco financing-structure disclosure.
